title: Paul Howard, the early Local 767 and its building on Central Avenue
summary: The early black local was nearly nothing until Paul Howard's membership drive and the purchase of an old house on Central Avenue.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: We were going to talk a little bit more about your involvement with the union. How did you -- you were a member of Local 767, right?
Did you say Paul Howard got you into it?
Yes, Paul Howard got me into the union. Well, of course, when I first came here in 1935, the union was,
you know -- there was a union. I don't even remember where it was located, but there was a union on Vernon or someplace, but it was nothing.
Someone said it started in somebody's garage.

I think so, I heard something to that effect. But it was just nothing, you know, just nothing. And Paul was very interested in building the union up. They had this old building -- they got this old building, later. They bought a building down on Central Avenue. And incidentally, Lee Young, Lee Young and his parents lived right next door to the union. They bought that house. I guess they lived there probably all that time. But the union bought this old house and made a union hall out of it. And that's the thing that got me into the union.

They had a drive on, to get people in, you know, involved in the union. At that time we had an awful lot of musicians. They were coming in here from every direction, you know. And most people, well like me, they had never belonged to a union. Well, in Lake Charles we didn't even have a union, and nobody had any intentions of setting one up, and I don't think today there's a union there. However, they are affiliated with Beaumont, Texas. I think that whatever happens in Beau -- in Lake Charles, is handled through the Beaumont, Texas union, you know.

But Paul Howard was instrumental in getting me into it, and he made it financially possible, because they had this drive where I think you paid $5.00 down and $5.00 a month or something, until you got your joining fee paid, you know.
